name: Office upgrade
desc: Better space, better kit, a kitchen people actually use.
pitch: Happier people, easier hiring.
lesson: Workplace quality is a retention tool. Compare its cost with what you pay recruiters every time someone leaves.

name: Automation line
desc: Robots, conveyors and software that let each operator do more.
pitch: Each operator produces about a fifth more once the line beds in.

risk.text: Integration bugs halted an automated line

lesson: Automation swaps a variable cost (labour) for a fixed one (capital). Margins widen when volume is high and get crushed when it falls — that is operating leverage.

name: Second shift
desc: Run the plant sixteen hours a day instead of eight.
pitch: A third more output from the same plant, at once.
lesson: Sweating an existing asset is the cheapest capacity there is — until maintenance and morale catch up with you.

name: Battery storage
desc: Store power when it is cheap and sell it when it is not.
pitch: Sell into the evening peak; win contracts that need firm power.
lesson: Storage turns an intermittent asset into a dispatchable one. The value is in the price spread, not the kilowatt-hours.

name: Regional brand campaign
desc: Six quarters of advertising across the region.
pitch: Awareness now, fading over a year and a half.
lesson: Advertising is an asset with a short life. The effect is strongest on day one and decays; budget for it as a recurring cost, not a one-off.

name: Global brand campaign
desc: One message, every market, two years.
pitch: Lifts brand everywhere you operate.
lesson: Brand spending pays back slowly and is hard to measure, which is exactly why it gets cut first in a downturn — and why competitors who keep spending gain share.

name: Celebrity sponsorship
desc: A household name wears your logo.
pitch: A household name fronting your brand. Awareness doubles overnight.
truth: The star’s agent is pushing hard because two other sponsors just walked. A scandal is brewing: roughly a one-in-ten chance each quarter that it breaks with your logo attached.

risk.text: Your celebrity sponsor is all over the news for the wrong reasons

lesson: Tying your brand to one person is key-person risk you cannot manage. When a deal is being pushed at you, ask who walked away from it first.

name: Customer success program
desc: People whose whole job is making customers succeed with what they bought.
pitch: Customers stay longer and buy more.
lesson: Keeping a customer is usually five times cheaper than winning one. Retention spending compounds; acquisition spending has to be repeated.

name: Pricing analytics
desc: Data on who pays what, and why.
pitch: Sharper prices and better-aimed sales effort.
lesson: A 1% better price falls straight to profit. Most companies know their costs to the cent and their customers’ willingness to pay not at all.

name: Sales enablement
desc: Playbooks, coaching and tooling for the sales team.
pitch: Every rep sells more.
lesson: Raising the output of the people you already have is cheaper than hiring more of them.

name: Franchise program
desc: Let others open your concept with their money.
pitch: Fee income and brand reach without the capex.

risk.text: A franchisee scandal hit your brand

lesson: Franchising is capital-light growth: you rent out the brand. The price is losing control of how it is run.

name: Ordering and delivery app
desc: Your own channel instead of paying a marketplace 25%.
pitch: More orders per location, direct customer relationships.
lesson: Owning the customer relationship is worth more than the margin a middleman takes — once you have the volume to justify building it.

name: Training academy
desc: Structured development for everyone, every quarter.
pitch: Skills rise, people stay.
lesson: Human capital is the only asset that appreciates when you invest in it and walks out when you do not.

name: Leadership bench
desc: A named successor for every key role, and time for them to learn it.
pitch: When someone leaves, the gap is small.
lesson: Key-person risk is a concentration risk like any other. You cannot stop people leaving; you can stop it being a crisis.

name: Culture and values program
desc: Deliberate effort on how the company works, not just what it does.
pitch: A company people do their best work in.
lesson: Culture is what people do when nobody is checking. It shows up in productivity, in attrition, and most of all in how a crisis goes.

name: Employee share plan
desc: Everyone owns a piece. Costs you 4% of the company.
pitch: People who own shares stay, and act like owners.
lesson: Equity compensation costs no cash, which makes it feel free. It is paid for in dilution — a real cost to every existing shareholder, including you.

name: Government affairs office
desc: People who know the regulators before you need them.
pitch: A seat at the table when rules are written.
lesson: In regulated industries the rules are part of the competitive landscape. Incumbents shape them; newcomers discover them.

name: Quality management system
desc: Measure defects, find causes, fix processes.
pitch: Fewer mistakes reach customers.
lesson: Quality is cheapest at the source. A defect costs 1 to prevent, 10 to catch, and 100 once the customer finds it.

name: ERP and systems overhaul
desc: Replace the spreadsheets and the twenty-year-old database.
pitch: One source of truth; lower overhead at scale.

risk.text: The ERP go-live went badly: orders lost, invoices wrong

lesson: Big-bang system replacements overrun more often than not. The payoff is real but late, and the risk is concentrated at go-live.

name: Cybersecurity program
desc: Monitoring, drills, patching, and someone whose job it is.
pitch: When the attack comes — and it will — it is an incident, not a catastrophe.
lesson: Security spending is insurance: its return is the disaster that did not happen, which never shows up in any report.

name: Competitive intelligence unit
desc: Analysts who watch rivals for a living.
pitch: See rivals’ numbers and moves before they land.
lesson: Strategy is choice under uncertainty. Reducing the uncertainty about what competitors will do is worth paying for.

name: Reliability engineering
desc: Redundancy, observability and an on-call rota that works.
pitch: Fewer outages, lower hosting bills.
lesson: For a subscription business, uptime is the product. Churn after an outage costs far more than the engineering to prevent it.

name: Fleet telematics
desc: Every vehicle tracked, every route optimised.
pitch: Less fuel, fewer empty miles.
lesson: In a thin-margin business, a few points of cost are the whole profit.

name: Knowledge platform
desc: Every past project searchable; every method reusable.
pitch: Juniors deliver like seniors.
lesson: A consulting firm’s only durable asset besides its people is what it has learned. Capture it or pay to relearn it.

name: Patent portfolio and legal defence
desc: File what you invent; keep lawyers on retainer.
pitch: A shield when someone sues, a sword when someone copies.
lesson: Patents rarely stop a determined competitor, but they change the negotiation when the lawsuits start.

name: Central research lab
desc: A team that works on next decade’s products, not next quarter’s.
pitch: Every R&D dollar and engineer goes a quarter further.
lesson: Research has increasing returns to scale and decreasing returns to impatience.

name: Next-generation platform
desc: Rebuild the core product for the next ten years.
pitch: A step-change in technology if every stage lands.
lesson: Staging an investment buys you an option at each gate: fund the next stage only if the last one worked. Money already spent is sunk and should not enter the decision.

name: Moonshot
desc: The thing that would redefine the industry, if it works.
pitch: One chance in five. If it lands, nothing else you do will matter as much.
lesson: A bet with a large positive expected value can still be a bad idea if losing it kills you. Size risky bets to what you can afford to lose.

name: Drug candidate
desc: One molecule, five gates, about five years.
pitch: Roughly one in eleven from preclinical to approval. Approved drugs earn 80% margins for a decade.
lesson: Value a pipeline by multiplying the prize by the chance of reaching it and discounting for time. Then run several candidates, because any single one will probably fail.

name: Process innovation program
desc: Engineers pointed at cost instead of features.
pitch: The same output from fewer inputs.
lesson: Product innovation wins customers; process innovation keeps the money. In commodity businesses the low-cost producer is the one left standing.

name: Low-cost offshore supplier
desc: Switch the bulk of purchasing to a new overseas source.
pitch: Same spec, 12% cheaper. Audited factory.
truth: The audit was signed by the supplier’s brother-in-law. Quality escapes and labour violations are likely — about a 6% chance each quarter that it ends up in the news.

risk.text: Your offshore supplier is in the news

lesson: A price far below the market is information. The saving is visible on day one; the risk you took on to get it shows up later, all at once.

name: Buy a key supplier
desc: Own the source of your biggest input.
pitch: Cheaper inputs, better quality, no more being squeezed.
lesson: Make-or-buy: owning a supplier captures its margin and secures supply, but adds fixed cost and removes your freedom to switch.

name: Supply-chain resilience
desc: Second sources and buffer stock for everything critical.
pitch: Disruptions pass you by.
lesson: Efficiency and resilience trade off. The leanest supply chain is the cheapest every year except the one that matters.

name: Decarbonisation program
desc: Measure emissions, cut them, prove it.
pitch: Lower energy bills later, better standing with customers and regulators.
lesson: Sustainability spending is partly a cost, partly an option on future regulation, and partly marketing. Know which part you are buying.

name: Community foundation
desc: Fund things in the cities you operate in.
pitch: Goodwill with the people whose goodwill you need.
lesson: Reputation is built slowly in good times and drawn down quickly in bad ones. It is a reserve, like cash.

name: Buy your headquarters
desc: Stop paying rent; own the building.
pitch: Saves about 6% a year on what you put in.
lesson: Owning property earns a landlord’s return. If your business earns more than that on its capital, the building is a poor use of it.

name: Signature campus
desc: An architect-designed headquarters with your name on it.
pitch: A talent magnet and a statement to the market that you have arrived.
truth: Running costs are 10% of the build cost every year, forever. The effect on hiring is small, and companies that build palaces start behaving as if they live in one.
lesson: Monuments are fixed costs that produce nothing. A new headquarters is one of the most reliable signs that a company has stopped watching its money.

name: Treasury bond ladder
desc: Park idle cash in government bonds of staggered maturity.
pitch: Earn a safe return on cash you do not need this year.
lesson: Idle cash has an opportunity cost. But cash you may need within a year should never be anywhere you cannot get it back at par.

name: Corporate venture bets
desc: Minority stakes in start-ups near your industry.
pitch: Most will fail. One might return the fund several times over.

hit.text: One of your venture bets was acquired

risk.text: Your venture portfolio has been written off

lesson: Venture returns follow a power law: a few winners pay for everything. That only works across a portfolio, and only with money you can lose.

name: Digital-asset treasury
desc: Hold part of the company’s cash in digital assets.
pitch: Cash loses 3% a year to inflation. This went up 80% last year.
truth: Eighty percent annual volatility, no cash flows, and your coins sit on an exchange that could fail. The odds favour losing most of it before you ever get the big payout.

hit.text: Your digital-asset holding tripled and you sold

risk.text: The exchange holding your digital assets has collapsed

lesson: Treasury’s job is to make sure the cash is there when payroll is due. Last year’s return is not a forecast, and speculation with operating cash is not treasury.

name: Aggressive tax structure
desc: Route profits through three countries and a partnership.
pitch: Perfectly legal. Everyone your size does it. Cuts your tax bill by a third.
truth: "Everyone" is being audited. Expect a challenge within a few years: back taxes, penalties and your name in the paper.

risk.text: Tax authorities are challenging your structure

lesson: Tax planning is legitimate; schemes sold on "everyone does it" are a loan from the tax authority at an unknown interest rate.

name: Hedging program
desc: Forward contracts on currencies, fuel and commodities.
pitch: Halves the effect of price and currency shocks, for a steady premium.
lesson: Hedging does not make money on average — it costs a little. What it buys is a narrower range of outcomes, which matters most to a company that cannot afford the bad tail.
